headline: Dyson won't explain $500 toothbrush component issue
summary: Dyson has acknowledged a “component issue” with its $500 toothbrush but won't say what went wrong, how many units are affected, or why it hasn't recalled the device.

claims.statement: Dyson has admitted a “component issue” with its $500 toothbrush but won't detail what went wrong.

sources.quote: admitting to a “component issue,” the company refuses to say what went wrong
Dyson admits a component issue but won't say what's failing

claims.statement: Wired reports Dyson also won't say how many units are affected, in how many countries, or why it won't recall the toothbrush.

sources.quote: how many units are affected in how many countries, and why it won’t recall its $500 AI toothbrush

claims.statement: Ars Technica frames the unexplained issue as a possible waterproofing problem.
